standard_prerequisites.name: Glueing data consisting of modules over the localizations with compatible transition isomorphisms come from a unique module whose localizations realize the given modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the module whose image under the functor can be compared with the given glued object.

standard_prerequisites.name: Two modules over the flat cover that become isomorphic after localizing at each of the elements are canonically isomorphic
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the first component of the glued object with the base change of the module produced by glueing.

standard_prerequisites.use: Together with the essential image statement, gives the equivalence of categories.

core_obligations: Take an object of the glued category given by its components and transition isomorphisms, and use the glueing statement for modules to produce a unique module together with isomorphisms from its localizations to the given components, recovering the transition data (proof lines 24776-24780).

Observe that the second component of the glued object and the base change of the produced module are both modules over the flat cover whose localizations at the elements are the same, so that they are canonically isomorphic (proof lines 24780-24784).

Conclude that the given glued object lies in the essential image of the functor, and combine this with the earlier statement that the other composite is isomorphic to the identity to obtain that the two functors are quasi-inverse equivalences of categories (proof lines 24784-24788).
proof_roadmap: Apply the glueing statement to the data of a glued object to get a module realizing its localizations (proof lines 24776-24780).
Compare the cover component of the object with the base change of that module and conclude they are canonically isomorphic (proof lines 24780-24784).
Read off the essential image and combine with the known composite to get the equivalence (proof lines 24784-24788).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a flat ring map and an ideal generated by finitely many elements whose ideal is the whole ring, the functor sending a module to its glued object and the functor sending a glued object to its global sections are quasi-inverse equivalences between modules and the glued category (statement lines 24767-24774). The proof takes an arbitrary glued object, uses the glueing statement for modules over a flat cover to produce a module realizing its localizations, identifies the cover component of the object with the base change of that module by comparing their localizations at the elements, and combines the resulting essential image statement with the known composite to conclude (proof lines 24776-24788). The comparison of the two cover components through their localizations is what makes the argument work in this degenerate case where the ideal is the whole ring.
